correctness.rationale: The full-gap 0 1^j 0 uniquely determines cyclic phase for all pairwise-distinct gap lengths. Immediate prefix and suffix occurrences with a shared full gap force the complete word, excluding four-or-more zeros and reducing three-zero candidates to exact gap pairs. One-zero and two-zero candidates follow from explicit edge dominance and gap predecessor/successor inequalities. Families are disjoint; their union and count are proved. A separately constructed cyclic-factor brute enumerator agreed in all 152 permutations with 2..5 distinct consecutive gaps and six irregular profiles; 2730 additional three-gap formula tests passed. Neither finite experiment establishes the unrestricted theorem.

originality.rationale: Fici–Restivo–Rizzo give general circular minimal forbidden factor automata and the Fibonacci special family, without the new distinct-gap classification. Akagi et al. give a general linear-string run-length encoded algorithm and type bounds, not an explicit cyclic all-r formula. The prior three-gap M+4 identity is covered and excluded from novelty. Novel mathematical content is a uniform at-most-three-zero theorem, parameter-uniform six-family antidictionary formula for arbitrary r, and explicit first ordering dependence with four gaps.

value.rationale: A complete and explicit circular antidictionary for every number of pairwise-distinct positive zero gaps is a natural symbolic classification (no bound on r or gap magnitudes). The phase-uniqueness lemma forces every minimal absent word to contain at most three zeros, converting an unbounded factor-language problem to cyclic predecessor/successor comparisons. The first sensitivity of count to cyclic order appears at four gaps despite identical gap multisets (10 versus 11), a non-obvious structural phenomenon. The result supports direct run-length-level factor analysis and reconstruction, without claiming an algorithmic speedup over general enumerators.
